newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds pare early gains to close flat.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds pare early gains to close flat.

text.p: Canadian bonds pared early gains to close little changed on Wednesday, as a drop in U.S. treasuries, a softer Canadian dollar and selling to lock in price gains weighed on the market, analysts said.

"Starting the day we did okay. Appearantly there were some buyers of the belly of the Canadian curve out of Europe," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist with Lehman Brothers. "With what little gains we had, there were people prepared to take profits."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$107.50 to yield 7.349 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 7.10 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 25 basis points from 27 basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canadian bonds began the session stronger on European buying, gains in U.S. treasuries and a rebound in the value of the Canadian dollar. The dollar weakened to a two-year low on Friday amid concern the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike rates in May.
But by the end of the session, investors were displaying a willingness to take profits on the Canadian dollar and bonds, Gregory said.

"The fact that there were sellers lined up when the currency got strong enough suggests to me that we haven't seen the end of this yet in terms of weakness in the currency and lackluster bond markets as a result," said Gregory.
Analysts said bond investors were looking ahead to the release of the U.S. producer price index report for March due out on Friday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.02 to C$101.18 to yield 6.829 percent, while the U.S. bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to six basis points from five basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.13 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.23 percent.
